metadata.title: Orthogonal Matching Pursuit: Recursive Function Approximation with Applications to Wavelet Decomposition
metadata.authors: Y. C. Pati, R. Rezaiifar, P. S. Krishnaprasad
metadata.venue: Proc. of the 27th Annual Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: None: PDF first page title and authors match the registry entry (Orthogonal Matching Pursuit; Pati, Rezaiifar, Krishnaprasad).

nodes.name: Dictionary
nodes.statement: Given a collection of vectors $D = \{x_n\}$ in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, $D$ is called a dictionary; the elements are assumed normalized $\|x_n\| = 1$. Define $V = \overline{\mathrm{Span}\{x_n\}}$ and $W = V^{\perp}$ in $\mathcal{H}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A dictionary is a collection of unit-norm vectors in a Hilbert space; $V$ is the closure of its span and $W$ is the orthogonal complement of $V$.

nodes.name: Optimal $N$-term approximation
nodes.statement: Let $V_N = \mathrm{Span}\{x_{n_1},\ldots,x_{n_N}\}$. Then $f_N$ is an optimal $N$-term approximation if $f_N = P_{V_N} f$; equivalently, iff $R_N f \in V_N^{\perp}$.
nodes.statement_clean: An $N$-term expansion is optimal when it equals the orthogonal projection of $f$ onto the span of the chosen dictionary atoms.

nodes.name: Auxiliary model for newly selected atom
nodes.statement: For the update from a $k$-th order to a $(k+1)$-th order model, decompose the new atom as $x_{k+1} = \sum_{n=1}^{k} b_n^k x_n + \gamma_k$ with $\langle \gamma_k, x_n \rangle = 0$ for $n=1,\ldots,k$. Then $\sum_n b_n^k x_n = P_{V_k} x_{k+1}$ and $\gamma_k = P_{V_k^{\perp}} x_{k+1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Decompose each newly selected atom into its projection onto the span of previously selected atoms plus an orthogonal residual $\gamma_k$.

nodes.name: Affine wavelet dictionary (Mexican-hat frame)
nodes.statement: $D = \{\psi_{m,n} : m,n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ with $\psi_{m,n}(t) = 2^{m/2}\,\psi(2^m t - n)$, where $\psi(t) = \left(\tfrac{4}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^{1/2}(t^2 - 1)\,e^{-t^2/2}$ is the second derivative of a Gaussian.
nodes.statement_clean: The dictionary used in the experiments consists of dilates and translates of the second-derivative-of-Gaussian (Mexican-hat) wavelet.

nodes.name: Sparse representation in a nonorthogonal dictionary
nodes.statement: Given $f \in \mathcal{H}$ and a (possibly overcomplete, nonorthogonal) dictionary $D = \{x_n\}$, compute a representation $P_V f = \sum_n a_n x_n$, ideally an optimal $N$-term approximation $f_N = P_{V_N} f$ for the chosen subset $\{x_{n_1},\ldots,x_{n_N}\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Approximate a signal as a sparse combination of dictionary atoms; ideally so that the partial expansion equals the orthogonal projection onto the span of the selected atoms.

nodes.name: Matching Pursuit (MP)
nodes.statement: Iterative greedy algorithm of Mallat and Zhang (1992) that picks at each step the dictionary atom most correlated with the current residual.
nodes.pseudocode: Init $R_0 f = f$, $f_0 = 0$, $k = 0$. (I) Compute $\{\langle R_k f, x_n\rangle\}$. (II) Pick $x_{n_{k+1}}$ with $|\langle R_k f, x_{n_{k+1}}\rangle| \geq \alpha \sup_n |\langle R_k f, x_n\rangle|$. (III) Set $f_{k+1} = f_k + \langle R_k f, x_{n_{k+1}}\rangle x_{n_{k+1}}$ and $R_{k+1} f = R_k f - \langle R_k f, x_{n_{k+1}}\rangle x_{n_{k+1}}$. (IV) $k \leftarrow k+1$; repeat until convergence.

nodes.name: MP energy-conservation identity
nodes.statement: Because $\langle R_{k+1} f, x_{n_{k+1}}\rangle = 0$ in MP, the residual norms satisfy $\|R_k f\|^2 = \|R_{k+1} f\|^2 + |\langle R_k f, x_{n_{k+1}}\rangle|^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: MP residual energy decreases at each step by the squared inner product with the selected atom.
assumptions: $\{R_k f\}$ is the residual sequence produced by MP on dictionary $D$

nodes.name: Suboptimality of MP at finite $N$
nodes.statement: After $N$ iterations MP only guarantees $R_N f \perp x_{n_{k+1}}$ (the last selected atom), not $R_N f \in V_N^{\perp}$, so $f_N$ is in general not the optimal $N$-term approximation. Figure 1 illustrates the suboptimality in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: MP is asymptotically convergent but its finite-$N$ output is generally not the orthogonal projection onto the span of the selected atoms.

nodes.name: Order-$k$ to order-$(k+1)$ coefficient update for OMP
nodes.statement: Using the auxiliary model (DP265.3), the correct update is $a_n^{k+1} = a_n^k - \alpha_k b_n^k$ for $n = 1,\ldots,k$ and $a_{k+1}^{k+1} = \alpha_k$, where $\alpha_k = \dfrac{\langle R_k f, x_{k+1}\rangle}{\|\gamma_k\|^2} = \dfrac{\langle R_k f, x_{k+1}\rangle}{\|x_{k+1}\|^2 - \sum_n b_n^k \langle x_n, x_{k+1}\rangle}$.
nodes.statement_clean: OMP rewrites the previous coefficients $a_n^k$ and adds a new coefficient $\alpha_k$ so that the new residual is orthogonal to all $k+1$ selected atoms.
assumptions: $k$-th order model $f = \sum_{n=1}^k a_n^k x_n + R_k f$ with $\langle R_k f, x_n\rangle = 0$ for $n \leq k$

nodes.name: OMP residual update and energy identity
nodes.statement: The OMP residual satisfies $R_k f = R_{k+1} f + \alpha_k \gamma_k$ and $\|R_k f\|^2 = \|R_{k+1} f\|^2 + |\alpha_k|^2 \|\gamma_k\|^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Like MP, the OMP residual energy decreases monotonically; the decrement is $|\alpha_k|^2 \|\gamma_k\|^2$.
assumptions: OMP update of PrP265.2 with auxiliary model DP265.3

nodes.name: Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP)
nodes.statement: Greedy algorithm that, after each atom selection, updates all coefficients so the residual is orthogonal to the entire span of the selected atoms.
nodes.pseudocode: Init $f_0 = 0$, $R_0 f = f$, $D_0 = \emptyset$, $\gamma_0 = 0$, $a_n = 0$, $k = 0$. (I) Compute $\{\langle R_k f, x_n\rangle : x_n \in D \setminus D_k\}$. (II) Select $x_{n_{k+1}}$ with $|\langle R_k f, x_{n_{k+1}}\rangle| \geq \alpha \sup_n |\langle R_k f, x_n\rangle|$. (III) If $|\langle R_k f, x_{n_{k+1}}\rangle| < \epsilon$, stop. (IV) Reorder by swapping $k+1 \leftrightarrow n_{k+1}$. (V) Solve $A_k b^k = v_k$ to get the auxiliary coefficients with $x_{k+1} = \sum_n b_n^k x_n + \gamma_k$. (VI) Set $\alpha_k = \langle R_k f, x_{k+1}\rangle / \|\gamma_k\|^2$, $a_n \leftarrow a_n - \alpha_k b_n^k$ for $n \leq k$, $a_{k+1} = \alpha_k$, $f_{k+1} = \sum_{n=1}^{k+1} a_n x_n$, $R_{k+1} f = f - f_{k+1}$, $D_{k+1} = D_k \cup \{x_{k+1}\}$. (VII) $k \leftarrow k+1$ and repeat (I)-(VII).

nodes.name: Compute residual inner products
nodes.statement: Compute $\{\langle R_k f, x_n\rangle : x_n \in D \setminus D_k\}$.

nodes.name: Select best atom
nodes.statement: Find $x_{n_{k+1}} \in D \setminus D_k$ with $|\langle R_k f, x_{n_{k+1}}\rangle| \geq \alpha \sup_n |\langle R_k f, x_n\rangle|$, $0 < \alpha \leq 1$.

nodes.name: Stopping check
nodes.statement: If $|\langle R_k f, x_{n_{k+1}}\rangle| < \epsilon$, stop and return the current model.

nodes.name: Reorder dictionary
nodes.statement: Apply the permutation swapping indices $k+1 \leftrightarrow n_{k+1}$ so that the newly selected atom becomes $x_{k+1}$.

nodes.name: Solve auxiliary linear system
nodes.statement: Compute $\{b_n^k\}$ with $x_{k+1} = \sum_{n=1}^k b_n^k x_n + \gamma_k$, $\langle \gamma_k, x_n\rangle = 0$, by solving the normal equations $A_k b^k = v_k$.

nodes.name: Update coefficients, model and residual
nodes.statement: Set $\alpha_k = \langle R_k f, x_{k+1}\rangle / \|\gamma_k\|^2$, $a_n \leftarrow a_n - \alpha_k b_n^k$ for $n \leq k$, $a_{k+1} = \alpha_k$, $f_{k+1} = \sum_{n=1}^{k+1} a_n x_n$, $R_{k+1} f = f - f_{k+1}$, $D_{k+1} = D_k \cup \{x_{k+1}\}$.

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: Increment $k \leftarrow k + 1$ and return to step (I).

nodes.name: Convergence of OMP (Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement: For $f \in \mathcal{H}$, let $R_k f$ be the OMP residuals. Then (i) $\lim_{k \to \infty} \|R_k f - P_W f\| = 0$; (ii) $f_N = P_{V_N} f$ for $N = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$.
nodes.statement_clean: OMP converges to the projection of $f$ onto the closed span of the dictionary, and at every step $f_N$ is the best approximation in the span of the selected atoms.
assumptions: $\{R_k f\}$ are residuals generated by OMP on dictionary $D$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement: Convergence (i) parallels the proof of Theorem 1 in Mallat-Zhang [3]. Optimality (ii) follows immediately from the orthogonality conditions $\langle R_k f, x_n\rangle = 0$ for $n \leq k$.

nodes.name: Convergence by parallel of Mallat-Zhang argument
nodes.statement: Apply the Mallat-Zhang convergence argument [3] to the OMP energy identity (PrP265.3) to conclude $\|R_k f - P_W f\| \to 0$.

nodes.name: Optimality from orthogonality conditions
nodes.statement: By construction $\langle R_N f, x_n\rangle = 0$ for $n = 1,\ldots,N$, so $R_N f \perp V_N$ and hence $f_N = P_{V_N} f$.

nodes.name: Finite-dictionary termination of OMP
nodes.statement: If $D$ has $M < \infty$ elements, OMP converges in no more than $M$ iterations to the projection of $f$ onto $\mathrm{Span}(D)$. MP does not possess this property.
nodes.statement_clean: On finite dictionaries OMP terminates in at most $|D|$ steps; MP does not.
conclusions: OMP terminates in at most $M$ iterations with $f_M = P_{\mathrm{Span}(D)} f$

nodes.name: Recursive update of residual inner products
nodes.statement: The inner products needed at each iteration may be computed recursively via $\langle R_k f, x_n\rangle = \langle f - f_k, x_n\rangle = \langle f, x_n\rangle - \sum_j a_j^k \langle x_j, x_n\rangle$.
nodes.statement_clean: Inner products with the residual decompose into precomputed inner products with $f$ minus a running sum involving current coefficients.

nodes.name: Nonsingularity of $A_k$ via stopping threshold
nodes.statement: The positive constant $\epsilon > 0$ used in step (III) of OMP guarantees that $A_k$ is nonsingular, so $b^k = A_k^{-1} v_k$ is well-defined.

nodes.name: Block-recursive inversion of the Gram matrix
nodes.statement: Writing $A_{k+1} = \begin{pmatrix} A_k & v_k \\ v_k^* & 1 \end{pmatrix}$, the block matrix inversion formula gives $A_{k+1}^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} A_k^{-1} + \beta b^k {b^k}^* & -\beta b^k \\ -\beta {b^k}^* & \beta \end{pmatrix}$, with $\beta = 1/(1 - v_k^* b^k)$. Hence $A_{k+1}^{-1}$ and $b^{k+1}$ are computed recursively from $A_k^{-1}$ and $b^k$.
nodes.statement_clean: The inverse Gram matrix and auxiliary coefficients can be updated by a rank-one block formula, avoiding a fresh inversion at each step.
conclusions: $b^{k+1}$ is computable from $A_k^{-1}$ and $b^k$ in $O(k)$ work

nodes.name: $\mathbb{R}^2$ illustration of MP suboptimality
nodes.statement: Two non-orthogonal vectors $x_1, x_2 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and a target $f \in \mathbb{R}^2$ (Figure 1): MP exhibits non-monotone convergence to $f$ in the span of $\{x_1, x_2\}$, while OMP achieves $R_2 f = 0$ in exactly two iterations.
nodes.statement_clean: A two-dimensional toy example showing OMP reaches the exact answer in two steps, MP does not.

nodes.name: Wavelet experiment, Example I
nodes.statement: Both OMP and MP applied to the signal of Figure 2(a) using the affine wavelet dictionary (DP265.4) of 351 atoms; OMP attains a prescribed residual energy in far fewer iterations (Figure 2(b)) and is roughly 3-8x cheaper in FLOPs than MP for the prescribed accuracy (Figure 4).
nodes.statement_clean: First experimental comparison: OMP needs fewer iterations and fewer FLOPs than MP on a wavelet representation problem.

nodes.name: Wavelet experiment, Example II (3-atom signal)
nodes.statement: For a signal lying in the span of three dictionary vectors (Figure 5(a)), OMP converges in exactly three iterations and MP is roughly 20x more expensive to reach the same residual.
nodes.statement_clean: Second experiment: when the signal admits an exact 3-atom representation, OMP recovers it in 3 steps; MP is dramatically more expensive.

nodes.name: OMP cheaper than MP on highly redundant dictionaries
nodes.statement: Without rigorous argument, the authors conjecture that OMP will be computationally cheaper than MP for very redundant dictionaries, since OMP exploits the redundancy to maximize per-step error reduction.
nodes.statement_clean: Conjecture: OMP outperforms MP on highly overcomplete dictionaries.
